models.what: the train CRAFTING BENCH: a small welded steel workbench with a wooden top inside a low back / end rail, a bolted-down bench vise, bench grinder and gauge / test box with its cable, and a wire-mesh lower shelf

conditioningImage.generator: codex-cli 0.163.0 built-in image_gen (model id not reported)

orientation.result: Meshy native frame kept (no rotation): +Y up, the front (gauge dials, vise screw) = +Z, the low rail at the back (-Z) and the +X end

models.transform: uniform scale to the runtime length, grounded (min y = 0), centred on x / z, baked into the vertices (identity node); no rotation, no geometry simplification
models.convention: metres at runtime size, +Y up, origin at the bottom centre of the footprint; +Z = the front (the side the player stands at), X along the wall it stands against (vise at -X, gauge box at +X)

fixtures.name: rail
fixtures.what: the low rail along the back and the +X end of the top (part of the top)

fixtures.name: vise
fixtures.what: the bench vise on its bolted base plate at the -X end (its screw handle reaches past the front edge)

fixtures.name: grinder
fixtures.what: the bench grinder on its bolted foot

fixtures.name: gauge-box
fixtures.what: the gauge / test box at the +X end (two dials, toggle switches), with its cable

looseItems.note: nothing rises above the worktop outside the fixture zones; the dark marks on the top are painted stains (flat); the lower shelf is empty

measureMethod.worktopY: top-down height map (5 mm): the most populated 1 cm band above 0.5 m, refined to the mean of the cells within 6 mm = the wooden top
measureMethod.worktop: the height-map columns / rows in which at least a quarter of the cells are within 8 mm of the worktop height (the top as far as it is seen from above, inside its rail); free = the largest rectangle made only of such cells (nothing stands in it)
measureMethod.fixtures: every height-map cell rising more than 12 mm over the worktop is assigned to a reviewed plan zone (rail / vise / grinder / gauge box); more than 2 cm2 of raised cells outside the zones stops the cook (prop rule 4: no loose item is baked into the bench)
measureMethod.shelfY: the same plateau measure with everything from 15 cm under the worktop up ignored = the wire-mesh lower shelf

models.what: the ROUTE RADAR device module: a field cabinet (round scope, lamps, vent, side handles, coiled power lead) carrying a mast-mounted antenna bar and a whip aerial; it stands on a hand truck's nose plate

conditioningImage.generator: codex-cli 0.163.0 built-in image_gen (model id not reported)

orientation.result: Meshy native frame kept (no rotation): +Y up, the console face = +Z

models.transform: fixed uniform scale, grounded (min y = 0), the cabinet footprint (the lowest 5 % of the height) centred on x / z, baked into the vertices (identity node); no rotation, no geometry simplification
models.convention: metres at runtime size, +Y up, origin at the bottom centre of the cabinet's footprint; +Z = the console face. On the hand truck the origin sits at (0, nose plate top, mountZ) in the dolly frame

measureMethod.mountZ: the truck's cooked model (assets/models/p7-hand-truck-t25.glb, at z -0.071268 in the dolly frame) sampled every 2 mm above its nose plate (top 0.073 m): frontmost z per 4 mm (x, y) cell; the module's samples must stay 4 mm in front of it in their own and the neighbouring cells; rounded up to a millimetre
measureMethod.radius: largest plan distance from the dolly origin of the mounted module's samples up to bodyTop (limit 0.36 m; a whip aerial may reach 0.4 m)
measureMethod.bodyTop: the top of the model without a whip aerial: 5 mm slabs from the top down are skipped while thinner than 3 cm both ways
measureMethod.face: from the base up, the run of 5 mm slabs in which the cabinet body (inside the footprint's width: no handles / leads) is at least 75 % as wide as the footprint = the cabinet / console front
measureMethod.footprint: the plan bounds of the lowest 5 % of the height (the cabinet's base)

models.what: the SENTRY ROOF TURRET: a belt-fed machine gun with a sensor pod and twin ammunition boxes in a U yoke on a bolted slew-ring base, with its power hose and junction box

conditioningImage.generator: codex-cli 0.163.0 built-in image_gen (model id not reported)

orientation.result: rotated a quarter turn about +Y (the raw barrel points -X): +Y up, +Z = the muzzle at rest

models.transform: scale 1; a quarter turn about +Y, origin on the yaw axis (the base flange's centre) at the flange's underside (min y = 0), baked into the vertices; the mesh's 284 separate shells sorted (none cut) into three nodes sharing one material; two flat caps added (the rear arm plates' open inner sides, which the tilt uncovers); the head's vertices are relative to its node at the tilt axis; no geometry simplification
models.convention: metres at runtime size, +Y up, origin on the yaw axis at the underside of the base ring; +Z = the muzzle at rest. Nodes: turret-base (fixed), turret-yoke (child of the scene root; yaw = rotation.y about its origin), turret-head (child of the yoke at pitchPivot; tilt = rotation.x about its origin, positive = muzzle down)

caps.what: the two rear arm plates' open inner sides (uncovered when the head tilts) closed with flat fans; texture coordinates taken from each plate's own outer face

measureMethod.split: connected shells (vertices welded by position); shells are seeded into base / yoke / head by where they are, the remaining small ones join the class of the nearest classified shell (nearest first); mirror twins must agree; the result must equal the reviewed shell / triangle counts
measureMethod.caps: each rear arm plate is an open shell whose boundary loop lies in its innermost plane: a triangle fan over that loop about its centre, wound to continue the shell's outside (facing the gun); each cap vertex takes the texture coordinate of the nearest vertex of the plate's own outer face (no new texture)
measureMethod.pitchPivot: chosen, not a modelled hinge: the lateral axis that lets the gun depress in front of the yoke (the modelled hub discs on the rear arms would only allow ~6 degrees before the nose meets the yoke floor)
measureMethod.pitchClear: column test on a 2 mm plan grid: the tilted head's underside against the top of the yoke + base, columns overlapping at rest (the mounts) left out; the largest whole-degree angle each way with at most 0.5 cm2 deeper than 1 mm. overPlane = the largest depression (within down) at which the head's lowest point (the barrel's tip) stays 10 mm above the mounting plane y = 0 (lowestAtDown: that point's height per angle)
measureMethod.muzzle: the centre of the head's vertices within 4 mm of its front end (the barrel's tip), at rest
measureMethod.yawAxis: the centre of the base flange's bounds (the slew rings agree within 4 mm)
